title.label: Notes as a work of art

content.label:
I have known about Bear for a while but never considered it because I expect end to end encryption a mandatory requirement for my notes app as I can’t be worrying about which notes to store there and which I shouldn’t. When Bear finally enabled the encryption with ADP in their sync, I immediately switched to it. And let me tell you, it has blown my mind. 

The app is a delectable writing and reading treat for anything you may want to keep. Every element on the screen is carefully crafted and presented with elegance for the user. I have give the sync to be reliable and am still discovering many new and cool features. Just recently they have implemented callouts and the implementation is a work of art.

If you care for privacy, elegance, and efficiency in a writing app, you have to try this on

I’ve been using bear as my go-to note taking app for over a year and it’s great. The syncing is seamless, interface is elegant, it’s super simple to use, and tags are so much better than folders. I would say the only drawbacks are the lack of tabs and exclusivity to apple devices. I go back and forth between Bear and Obsidian now but this app hands down has better apple functionality. I know it’s easy for writers to get lost in the bells and whistles, distracted by all of the different programs that make you think ‘Oh this one will get me to write more’. Well Bear did actually get me to write more (this is the first review I’ve left for an app), and though it might not have every feature you could ever want, it is definitely the best at what its trying to be–streamlined, elegant, and practical.

Since the recent update, the app has managed to lose written entries during general screen refreshes when switching between apps. The ability to start an entry and revisit the app between app screens wasn’t a problem until now. With several apps facing vulnerability issues due to Apple’s lack of awareness to exploits used against their customers it’s concerning that any app, especially one touting the best security measures preventing anyone including themselves from accessing personal data would allow for a vulnerability to present itself in this manner. This was a good app until this occurred but, will be expecting an update to bring the app back to the level it was at in terms of ensuring that entries will always remain secure. Run some tests on your software and ensure that entries will not be affected with the next update. Take into consideration as well that the app is running on a paid subscription with features that are an added benefit that doesn’t necessarily need to be used in securing data but, every single entry using the encryption method has to be checked now too to ensure they haven’t been deleted as well. It’s software. It isn’t always perfect but, at least the app developer (and other customers who may be experiencing similar if not the same problem) can be made alerted to the issue.

Been using bear on subscription for years now. It is a fantastic tool and has become my library of hundreds of notes. 

BUT even after these years of use, it’s still lacking one key feature for someone like myself with hundreds and hundreds of notes: you can’t search the note itself on an iPhone! You can search the library for a key word, and that global search will search the note too, but when you select the result of interest, your 10,000 word note has no highlighted result from the search. And it’s not like basic word editors (or the Mac version of Bear) where you can then search within the note.

Second, because I rely so heavily upon it…and because it has no possible way for use when I’m at work on a PC, I have a serious workflow breakdown. I have to write in OneNote or some other editor, then copy-paste from that editor on my Mac or iPhone to get it into Bear, and it usually hates the formatting. (Or I email myself.) A web interface has been in the works for years but seems like it’s a long, long way from release.

Yes, I recommend Bear, but if those two issues were solved it would make using it just that much better.

However, I cannot understand what I’m paying for. It’s not for improvements, because the developers just let feature requests hang for years, and refuse to commit to timelines. It makes me think they aren’t actually serious. The Craft app, on the other hand, has had substantial monthly updates since inception, and every update is polished and well thought through. I’ve switched over because I prefer to use products that the developers actually improve.
